paper: Mutation-Guided Unit Test Generation with a Large Language Model
baseline: EvoSuite and vanilla prompt-based LLM generation
metrics: Mutation score, coverage-related analysis, live/uncovered mutants
main_result: MutGen incorporates surviving-mutant feedback into prompts and significantly outperforms EvoSuite and vanilla prompting in mutation score.
limitation: Some mutants remain live or uncovered; effectiveness depends on mutation operators; coverage alone can be misleading.
useful_for_our_study: Strong evidence for using mutation score as a main outcome and for discussing why high branch coverage is not enough.

paper: CodaMosa: Escaping Coverage Plateaus in Test Generation with Pre-trained Large Language Models
model: CodaMosa with OpenAI Codex plus SBST
dataset: 486 benchmark programs/functions used for SBST evaluation
main_result: CodaMosa uses Codex-generated examples when SBST coverage stalls and improves coverage over standard SBST on many subjects.
limitation: Mostly coverage-focused and Python-based; it does not directly evaluate Java/JUnit or mutation score for the planned setting.
useful_for_our_study: Useful background for coverage plateaus and for comparing pure LLM generation with search-based test generation.

paper: Effective Test Generation Using Pre-trained Large Language Models and Mutation Testing
model: MuTAP, mutation-augmented prompting with pre-trained code LLMs
dataset: Synthetic buggy code and benchmark programs used for mutation-based test generation
baseline: Baseline LLM prompting and traditional automated test generation approaches
metrics: Mutation score, bug detection, coverage-related measures
main_result: MuTAP augments prompts with surviving-mutant information and reports improved mutation score and fault detection compared with baseline prompting.
limitation: Results depend on mutant quality and iterative prompting; evidence is mainly outside Java/JUnit.
useful_for_our_study: Supports the gap that LLM tests need mutation-based assessment, not only coverage.

paper: LLMs and Prompting for Unit Test Generation: A Large-Scale Evaluation
model: Four LLMs with five prompting techniques
dataset: 690 Java classes and about 216300 generated tests
main_result: Large-scale evaluation shows that model and prompt choices strongly affect generated unit-test quality and that LLM tests must be assessed across multiple metrics.
limitation: Generation quality varies across prompts/models; high volume does not guarantee correctness or strong fault detection.
useful_for_our_study: Useful for justifying a fixed prompt protocol and for reporting compile/pass, coverage, and mutation-style quality separately.

paper: HITS: High-Coverage LLM-Based Unit Test Generation via Method Slicing
model: HITS, LLM-based method slicing test generation
dataset: Complex focal methods from Java projects used by prior test-generation studies
baseline: Current LLM-based test-generation methods and EvoSuite
main_result: Method slicing reduces the reasoning scope for complex methods and significantly improves line and branch coverage over existing LLM and SBST baselines.
limitation: Primarily optimizes coverage; mutation/fault-detection evidence is less central than coverage evidence.
useful_for_our_study: Directly supports the project focus on medium-complexity Java methods/classes and branch coverage.

paper: LLMs for Automated Unit Test Generation and Assessment in Java: The AgoneTest Framework
dataset: Classes2Test dataset mapping Java classes under test to corresponding test classes
baseline: Human-written tests and different LLM/prompting configurations
metrics: Compilation/execution status, coverage, mutation score, test smells, defect detection
main_result: AgoneTest provides an automated Java evaluation framework; for compilable generated tests, LLM tests can match or exceed human-written tests in coverage and defect detection.
limitation: Framework paper; exact results depend on dataset, prompting strategy, and compile-success filtering; final experiment still needs its own controlled Java/Python subjects.
useful_for_our_study: Useful evidence that Java unit-test generation requires assessment infrastructure, not only prompt output collection.

paper: An initial investigation of ChatGPT unit test generation capability
model: OpenAI ChatGPT / OpenAI LLM parameter variants
dataset: 33 Java programs with 33 generated test sets per program
baseline: Traditional automated Java unit-test generation tools from prior work
metrics: Code/line coverage, mutation score, test execution success rate
main_result: ChatGPT-generated Java tests showed performance similar to traditional automated Java test generators across the reported metrics.
limitation: Early and relatively simple setup; generated code was not manually analyzed or repaired in depth.
useful_for_our_study: Direct Java evidence for comparing LLM-generated tests with traditional automated test generation using coverage and mutation score.

paper: Advancing Code Coverage: Incorporating Program Analysis with Large Language Models
baseline: SBST and LLM-enhanced baselines such as Pynguin, CodaMosa, and ChatTester
main_result: TELPA uses static/dynamic program analysis and counterexamples to guide LLMs toward hard-to-cover branches, reporting large branch-coverage improvements.
limitation: Python-focused and coverage-focused; does not by itself answer Java/JUnit mutation-score questions.
useful_for_our_study: Useful for explaining hard-to-cover branches and why context/program analysis can matter for branch coverage.

paper: Automated Unit Test Generation via Chain of Thought Prompt and Reinforcement Learning from Coverage Feedback
model: TestCTRL, CodeLlama-7B fine-tuned with CoT and RL from coverage feedback
dataset: Java unit-test generation benchmarks including Defects4J-style subjects and generated CoT data
baseline: State-of-the-art LLM prompting and automated test-generation baselines
metrics: Validity/naturalness, line coverage, branch coverage, bug detection
main_result: TestCTRL uses coverage feedback as a reward signal and improves generated unit tests on coverage and bug-detection-oriented measures.
limitation: Requires fine-tuning/RL infrastructure and feedback collection; not directly comparable to a simple one-shot GPT prompt unless separated as a stronger baseline.
useful_for_our_study: Supports the idea that coverage feedback can improve LLM tests, while this project can evaluate a simpler fixed-prompt GPT setting.

paper: Impact of code context and prompting strategies on automated unit test generation with modern general-purpose large language models
model: Six general-purpose LLMs including Gemini 2.5 Pro
dataset: 12 custom Python methods designed to reduce data leakage
baseline: Software practitioner baseline and alternative context/prompting strategies
metrics: Branch coverage, mutation score, compilation success, cost
main_result: Docstrings and sequential prompting improve test quality; best prompting reached high branch coverage and Gemini 2.5 Pro reached strong mutation score compared with the practitioner baseline.
limitation: Small custom Python dataset; sequential prompting increases cost; models still miss robustness cases such as None, inf, and NaN.
useful_for_our_study: Strong supporting evidence for comparing LLM tests with human/student tests and for tracking branch coverage, mutation score, compile success, and cost tradeoffs.

paper: ChatGPT vs SBST: A Comparative Assessment of Unit Test Suite Generation
dataset: Java unit-test suite generation benchmark used for comparison with EvoSuite
metrics: Correctness, readability, code coverage, bug detection capability
main_result: The study compares ChatGPT and EvoSuite across correctness, readability, coverage, and bug detection, showing different strengths and weaknesses of LLM-based and SBST-generated tests.
limitation: Does not replace a controlled comparison with student-written tests; metric strengths may differ by benchmark and prompt setup.
useful_for_our_study: Useful baseline evidence for discussing ChatGPT versus established automated test-generation tools.

paper: Using Large Language Models to Generate JUnit Tests: An Empirical Study
baseline: Comparison across models, contexts, and benchmark settings
metrics: Compilation rate, test correctness, test coverage, test smells
main_result: Codex achieved over 80 percent coverage on HumanEval, but all models performed poorly on EvoSuite SF110 with very low coverage; generated tests also had test smells.
limitation: Strong performance on simple tasks does not transfer to harder Java benchmark code; generated JUnit tests may compile poorly or contain test smells.
useful_for_our_study: Directly supports the Java/JUnit scope and motivates selecting medium-complexity subjects rather than trivial examples.

paper: Evaluating LLM-Generated Unit Tests with Mutation Testing: ChatGPT vs DeepSeek
dataset: Six Java classes from Defects4J with different cyclomatic complexity levels
baseline: Comparison between ChatGPT and DeepSeek generated test suites
metrics: Mutation coverage, mutation score, compilation/runtime failures, qualitative failure analysis
main_result: DeepSeek produced more stable and mutation-effective suites, while ChatGPT generated valid suites for a wider range of classes; failures were mainly semantic rather than purely complexity-driven.
limitation: Small dataset with six classes; results may not generalize across projects or prompts.
useful_for_our_study: Direct evidence for using mutation score on Java classes and for analyzing semantic failures in LLM-generated tests.

paper: Call-Chain-Aware LLM-Based Test Generation for Java Projects
dataset: Defects4J classes and additional Java GitHub projects
baseline: Recent LLM-based test generation baselines such as PANTA
main_result: CAT uses backward call-chain analysis to provide usage/context information and reports improved line and branch coverage over baselines.
limitation: Preprint evidence; focuses mostly on coverage and depends on project call-chain extraction quality.
useful_for_our_study: Useful Java evidence that project context and call chains affect branch coverage for generated tests.

paper: KTester: Leveraging Domain and Testing Knowledge for More Effective LLM-based Test Generation
model: KTester, LLM generation with injected project/testing knowledge
metrics: Pass rate, coverage, test quality and human-evaluation-oriented measures
main_result: KTester injects project and testing knowledge into prompts and improves LLM-based unit-test generation quality over baseline prompting.
limitation: Accepted/preprint source should be marked when cited; benefits depend on the availability and quality of extracted project knowledge.
useful_for_our_study: Supports the gap around context quality and motivates documenting prompt inputs and available code context in the later experiment.
